name: IP Classification (under test)
summary: Classifies IP addresses as scanners, C2 and malware families, crawlers, anonymizers and non-routable space.
description:
Answers why an IPv4 address showed up in a log or a graph: an internet-wide scanner, C2 infrastructure of a known framework or malware family, a search-engine crawler or AI bot, an anonymizer (VPN entry point, Tor exit, open proxy, iCloud Private Relay), or space that should never be routed. One plugin; no account or API key.

## Plugins

### IP Classification
- **Runs on:** selected IP Address nodes. IPv4 only: IPv6 values and nodes that are not IP Addresses are skipped and reported in the summary.
- **Adds:** properties on each IP node, and for each C2 match a Tool or Malware node linked from the IP with a `used as C2` edge. A public address that no list names is left untouched rather than stamped with an empty verdict.

| Property | Values |
|---|---|
| `ip_scope` | `private`, `loopback`, `cgnat`, `link_local`, `multicast`, `reserved`, `documentation`, `benchmark` (special-use ranges), or `unallocated` (bogon space). Omitted for ordinary public addresses. |
| `scanner` | the scanning service, e.g. `shodan`, `censys`, `tenable`, `binaryedge` |
| `crawler` | the crawler or bot, e.g. `googlebot`, `bingbot`, `applebot`, `gptbot`, `claudebot` |
| `anonymizer` | e.g. `nordvpn_entry`, `mullvad_entry`, `tor_exit_node`, `socks_proxy`, `icloud_private_relay` |
| `c2_family` | e.g. `cobalt_strike`, `sliver`, `remcos` |
| `tags` | the categories that matched: `scanner`, `c2`, `crawler`, `anonymizer`, and `bogon` whenever `ip_scope` is set |
| `scanner_source`, `crawler_source`, `anonymizer_source`, `c2_source` | the list each value came from, pinned to the commit it was read at when the list is hosted on GitHub |
| `scanner_first_seen`, `scanner_last_seen`, and the same for `crawler_`, `anonymizer_`, `c2_` | when the list first and last named the address (ISO 8601) |

Values are lowercase `snake_case`, and one address can carry several. When a scanner matches and the node has no `organization`, the scanner's value is written there.

- **C2 nodes.** Each C2 family becomes either a `threat.tool` node (C2 frameworks, and tools such as GoPhish, XMRig, BurpSuite and MobSF) or a `threat.malware` family node (RATs and the ShadowPad backdoor), with first and last seen dates. The `used as C2` edge carries the source list and the snapshot date.
- **Seen dates only widen.** A later run never narrows what an earlier one recorded: `first_seen` only moves earlier and `last_seen` only moves later.
- **VPN values end in `_entry`.** VPN providers publish their connection endpoints, not their egress addresses, so a VPN value names an entry point. For every anonymizer value, the address is not the person.

## What it recognizes

- **Scanners (22):** Shodan, Censys, Tenable, BinaryEdge, Stretchoid, Hunter, Quake, FOFA, ZoomEye, LeakIX, Netlas, ONYPHE, Criminal IP, Bitsight, Palo Alto Expanse, Recorded Future, Mandiant, Group-IB, VirusTotal, Intrinsec, Shadowserver, Rapid7.
- **C2 and malware (36):** as tools, Cobalt Strike, Sliver, Metasploit, Mythic, Havoc, Brute Ratel C4, Covenant, Empire, Posh, Caldera, Deimos, NimPlant, Viper, Villain, Supershell, RedGuard, PANDA, Hak5 Cloud C2, Unam Web Panel, GoPhish, XMRig, BurpSuite and MobSF; as malware, Sectop, Quasar, Remcos, njRAT, NanoCore, DcRAT, AsyncRAT, Gh0st, XtremeRAT, DarkComet, NetBus, Hookbot and ShadowPad.
- **Crawlers and AI bots:** Googlebot, Google special crawlers, Google user-triggered fetchers, Bingbot, Applebot, GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot.
- **Anonymizers:** VPN entry points of NordVPN, Mullvad, AirVPN, Privado, Surfshark, IVPN, VyprVPN and TorGuard; Tor exit nodes; SOCKS and SSL proxies; iCloud Private Relay.
- **Non-routable:** the special-use ranges of RFC 6890, answered locally, and unallocated (bogon) space from Team Cymru's full bogon list.

## Requirements

None: no account, no API key, no settings. Runs in the web app and on desktop.

## What it contacts

Only `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Vineyard-Intelligence/ip-observation-history/main`. A run reads `index.json` once (about 12 KiB) and one shard per distinct first octet (/8) among the selected public addresses (about 2 KiB each), so GitHub sees which /8 blocks were looked up, not the addresses themselves. Special-use ranges are answered without reading a shard. The addresses being classified are never contacted, and neither are the publishers of the lists.

Without network access the run still reports special-use scope and says that address data was unavailable. A shard that cannot be read is reported in the summary and does not stop the run.

## Data and licences

The bundle embeds no address lists, only the C2 family metadata that maps each family to a Tool or Malware node (snapshot of 2026-10-24). Address data comes from ip-observation-history, which collects published lists: OpenFilters internet-scanners (https://github.com/OpenFilters/internet-scanners), HL-SOC C2-Tracker (https://github.com/HL-SOC/C2-Tracker), FireHOL, Team Cymru, and vendors that publish their own crawler or VPN ranges. The full source table, with the address of every list, is in the ip-observation-history README: https://github.com/Vineyard-Intelligence/ip-observation-history

A value records that a published list named the address during the dates given; the matching `*_source` field names that list so the claim can be checked against it.

## Source

https://github.com/Vineyard-Intelligence/pluginpack-ip-classification (Apache-2.0)

There is no bundler: `node build.mjs` fills `src/template.mjs` with `src/dataset.json` to produce `dist/pack.mjs`, and `node scripts/gen-manifest.mjs` writes `plugins/ip-classification.manifest.json` from it. `npm test` runs the tests.
